title: Mass on a spring: simple harmonic motion (সরল স্পন্দন গতি)
placement: Book pages 188–190, topic 7.1 সরল স্পন্দন গতি: next to চিত্র ৭.০১ (a block on a spring, positions 0–9) on page 189.
description: A mass on a vertical spring (pages 188–190, topic 7.1, beside চিত্র ৭.০১): an open-coil steel spring with machine loops hangs from a retort stand's arm, a hanger of slotted brass 250 g masses on it and a metre rule in cm behind, on a teak bench under a light blue-grey backdrop, seen from a three-quarter view 22° above with the stand turned toward the camera. A follow camera keeps a fixed window round the mass and its travel. The student pulls the mass down (a drag, the arrow keys or the big numbered action button) and lets go: it oscillates about its সাম্যাবস্থা (dashed line) between two green lines marked v = 0, with বিস্তার a marked, the coils opening and bunching and an outlined blue velocity arrow beside it; time runs 5 times slower than real (said on the picture). The panel: rows of words for the mass m (0.25, 0.5, 1 kg) and the spring constant k (100, 200, 400 N/m), a live graph of x, v or the acceleration over four periods with a crimson tick at each whole period and a dashed ±a band, K and U bars that trade under their constant dashed total, one result line (T and f) and a rule that grows with what the student finds: T = 2π√(m/k), the same T for another amplitude, a longer T for more mass, a shorter one for a stiffer spring. Test: 5 questions (the energy at an end, read off the x–t graph where v is greatest, when the same phase first returns, read T off a graph and give f, twice the pull), every wrong choice with its own note. Phone-first, Bangla and English.
